conventions.convention: The equivariant setting assumes AC, a characteristic-zero coefficient field, a finite product of complex general linear groups, and bounded algebraically constructible complexes on separated finite-type complex varieties.

The normalized equivariant dualizing object restricts to the ordinary dualizing object; a smooth complex d-fold has ω_X^G = k_X[2d]. H_j^{BM,G}(X;k) = Hom(k_X,ω_X^G[-j]), with stable ordinary Borel value H_{j+2b}^{BM}(X×_G U;k), where b = dim_C U − dim_C G.

The diagonal Thom class is normalized by the positive complex normal-fibre generator. The refined operation retains support and drops Borel–Moore degree by twice the complex middle dimension; it does not assert purity of a singular support embedding or invertibility of its exchange mate.

The first coordinate is the categorical source. Matching corners multiply by a*b = h_*Δ_{X_j}^!(a⊠b), in Borel–Moore degree p+q−2d_j; nonmatching corners multiply to zero. A class of Borel–Moore degree p in corner (i,j) has algebra degree d_i+d_j−p.

For L_i = f_{i!}k[d_i], Ext degree r corresponds to Borel–Moore degree d_i+d_j−r. Shifted source-first composition is α*β = β[r]∘α, without an additional sign; identities correspond to positive diagonal fundamental classes.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC and the supplied analytic constructible six-functor hypotheses, for morphisms q:A→M and u:B→M with M smooth of pure complex dimension d, refined middle-diagonal pullback on support A×B is induced by the mate a* q!→b! u* after tensor evaluation and dualizing transitivity. It equals cap product with the positive diagonal Thom class, drops Borel–Moore degree by 2d on singular or nontransverse supports, respects ordered iteration, and gives Euler-class cap product for zero-section self-intersection.

With AC, characteristic-zero coefficients and a product of complex general linear groups, H_j^{BM,G}(X;k)=Hom(k_X,ω_X^G[-j]) uses the normalized dualizing object. For finitely many proper equivariant maps f_i:X_i→E with smooth pure-dimensional sources, source-first convolution is a*b=h_*Δ_{X_j}^!(a⊠b), of Borel–Moore degree p+q−2d_j and corner algebra degree d_i+d_j−p; nonmatching corners multiply to zero.

Under the stated AC-qualified equivariant constructible correspondence hypotheses, putting L_i=f_{i!}k_{X_i}[d_i], for every integer r and every pair (i,j) there is a natural isomorphism Φ_{ij}^r:Hom(L_i,L_j[r])→H_{d_i+d_j−r}^{BM,G}(Z_{ij};k). The groups are degreewise finite-dimensional; the isomorphism is equivariant-cohomology linear, compatible with Borel enlargement, and natural in constructible coefficient morphisms before orientation. No semismallness, decomposition theorem, purity, or smoothness of E or Z_{ij} is required.

For the data and maps Φ of the Ext/Borel–Moore theorem, α:L_i→L_j[r] and β:L_j→L_k[s] satisfy Φ_{ik}^{r+s}(β[r]∘α)=Φ_{ij}^r(α)*Φ_{jk}^s(β), where the right product is geometric convolution. Identities map to diagonal classes, giving a unital graded algebra isomorphism on the direct sum of all corners, with nonmatching products zero.

Under AC, for any finite loopless quiver, including parallel and opposite arrows, the stable graded complete-flag incidence space X_ν→B_ν is a complex algebraic vector bundle with smooth total space, π_ν:X_ν→E_V is projective, and all middle-forgetting projections are proper. The preceding equivariant Ext/convolution theorems apply with d_ν=dim_C X_ν and L_ν=Rπ_{ν!}k[d_ν], without smoothness or transversality of fibre products. Vector-bundle and flag-bundle projections have complex-oriented pullbacks; zero-section self-intersection is top-Chern-class cap product.

concerns.concern: Proof step 6.1 calls d_i+d_j−r and d_j+d_k−s the “corner degrees.” These are the incoming Borel–Moore degrees; the corner algebra degrees fixed by the Definition are r and s. The calculation itself is correct, but this terminology contradicts the declared grading convention.

Verification step 3.1 says “The corner degrees are … 2 for α … and … 0 for β.” These are Borel–Moore degrees. Their corner algebra/Ext degrees are −1 and 1 under the cited Definition. The numerical computation and product are correct; the degree labels need clarification.

The supported Thom proof constructs a morphism on arbitrary supports without claiming the support embedding itself is pure.
